Notorious Bega schoolgirl killer Leslie Camilleri has been hospitalised after being assaulted by inmates in a new correctional facility.

Camilleri, now in his mid-50s, was recently transferred to the Ravenhall Correctional Centre – a medium-security, all-male facility in Melbourne’s outer west – where he was assaulted by two fellow prisoners who knew of his crimes, according to a source with knowledge of the incident who is not authorised to speak publicly.

In a statement, a spokesperson at the Department of Justice and Community Safety said the incident occurred between three prisoners on June 17.

They confirmed a prisoner had been taken to hospital but declined to comment further on the incident.

“No other prisoners or staff were injured.”

In December 2013, Camilleri, then 43, was jailed for 28 years for the murder of 13-year-old Prue Bird who had disappeared from her home in Glenroy, in Melbourne’s northern suburbs, in 1992.

At the time, Victorian Supreme Court Justice Elizabeth Curtain said she was satisfied that Camilleri – who was already serving two life sentences without parole for raping and murdering Bega schoolgirls Lauren Barry and Nichole Collins in 1997 – and two other men had abducted and murdered Bird.

She said Camilleri and the two others had abducted a defenceless 13-year-old from her home in circumstances that must have been terrifying for her.

His defence barrister John Kelly told the court that Camilleri had tried his best to remember where he had left Bird’s body, but his memory had been affected by drug-taking at the time. During the time of offending, Camilleri was on parole after spending time in jail in Queensland.

A father of four, Camilleri had claimed he put Bird face down on the back seat of his car and tied her arms and legs with electrical cables before driving around for several hours. He said when he later pulled over to the side of the road, he realised she was dead.

The hospital to which Camilleri was taken has been contacted for comment.
